negative_findings.description: No Hungarian systemic bank appears to publish a supplier/vendor register, procurement page or tender portal on its own site. Searches combining bank names with 'beszállító', 'szállító', 'közbeszerzés', 'pályázat' returned factoring products (MBH Beszállítói Faktoring) rather than procurement disclosures.
negative_findings.result_summary: The term 'beszállítói' in HU banking web content overwhelmingly denotes supply-chain-finance products, not the bank's own suppliers — a strong false-friend term for this cell.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: vendor identity must be reconstructed from voluntary announcements, annual-report outsourcing notes and vendor-side claims, not from any procurement disclosure.

negative_findings.description: Bank name queries in Hungarian are dominated by consumer-facing aggregator/tabloid coverage (penzcentrum.hu, promotions.hu, index.hu tag pages) about fees, outages and warnings.
negative_findings.result_summary: Generic queries like 'K&H bank hírek' surface consumer news noise; precision requires pairing the bank name with terms such as 'bevezetés', 'rendszer', 'együttműködés', 'partner', 'kiszervezés'.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection queries must be term-constrained or the pipeline will be flooded with irrelevant retail-banking noise.

negative_findings.description: The MBH extraordinary-disclosure page slug could not be confirmed to a single canonical form; the search snippet showed a URL that may be a truncated or altered variant.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as a candidate with a caveat rather than asserting reachability; no fetch was performed to confirm.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A deterministic verification pass must resolve the real slug from the /befektetoi hub before scheduling collection, or the source will look dead when it is not.

negative_findings.description: No K&H Bank vendor/core-banking supplier announcement was found in either language during this pass; K&H (KBC group) appears to communicate technology changes mainly as product launches and maintenance notices.
negative_findings.result_summary: K&H technology-supplier identification will likely require the indirect route (maintenance notices, KBC group reports, conference speaker lists) rather than a press release.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations for coverage of one of the eight target banks and justifies prioritising indirect sources for it.

negative_findings.description: Gránit Bank does not appear to run a page labelled 'sajtószoba'; its public communication seems routed through the 'Befektetőknek' investor section and BÉT filings.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searching 'granitbank.hu sajtószoba' returned the investor page and third-party company registries instead of a press room.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design for Gránit must target the IR/BÉT path, not a press-room crawler template reused from the other seven banks.

coverage_gaps.description: Erste, UniCredit and CIB are subsidiaries of foreign groups (Erste Group, UniCredit S.p.A., Intesa Sanpaolo); group-level press rooms and annual reports were not scouted in this cell and may carry the Hungary-relevant technology decisions.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a follow-up cell covering parent-group newsrooms and annual reports (Erste Group, UniCredit, Intesa Sanpaolo, KBC for K&H, RBI for Raiffeisen) filtered for Hungary mentions.

coverage_gaps.description: Most bank press rooms were located but their historical pagination depth and any RSS/JSON feeds were not established; only CIB showed an explicit year-archive pattern and MBH a date-slug pattern.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a structural probe per domain: find pagination parameters, RSS/sitemap.xml, and earliest retrievable release date; record the crawl recipe per bank.

coverage_gaps.description: Pillar 3 / nyilvánosságra hozatal disclosures and ICT/outsourcing registers under DORA were not systematically located per bank; only OTP's 'Nyilvánosságra hozatal' page surfaced.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate each bank's Pillar 3 / nyilvánosságra hozatali dokumentum page and check whether DORA-driven ICT third-party arrangements are described; this is the highest-value untapped disclosure vein for vendor identity.

coverage_gaps.description: The statutory e-beszámoló filing portal (company annual accounts) was not reached in this pass, though third-party registries (OPTEN, Nemzeti Cégtár) appeared as pointers.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout the official company-accounts filing portal and the commercial registries as an indirect route to subsidiary-level IT service company relationships.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank-owned non-web channels — LinkedIn company pages, YouTube channels, developer/API portals and careers pages — were not scouted; job ads and API docs are among the most reliable indirect reveals of the technology stack in use.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a sub-cell for careers/job postings and developer/API portals of the eight banks, in Hungarian ('állás', 'fejlesztő', 'rendszer'), as an indirect vendor-detection channel.

brief: All eight Hungarian systemic banks maintain a self-published press room and an investor/annual-report section, and these are reachable, stable, and mostly crawlable without authentication — CIB and MBH even expose predictable per-release URL patterns. However, none of them discloses suppliers systematically: vendor identity appears only when the bank chooses to announce a win (OTP–iGCB Intellect Digital Core, Magyar Bankholding/MBH–Thought Machine) or when it is buried in annual-report outsourcing notes and terms-and-conditions documents. The highest-yield collection design therefore pairs each bank's own press room and annual report with three indirect confirmers: vendor-side and trade-press announcements (FinTechZone in Hungarian, FinTech Futures in English), the Portfolio Banking Technology conference programme as a bank–vendor relationship roster, and operational artefacts such as K&H's maintenance notices. Beware the false friend 'beszállítói', which in Hungarian bank content means supply-chain finance products rather than the bank's own suppliers.
